items.text: Every task has an owner and a due date
Each role's requirement and sketch fields are complete
The sketches meet at the named interfaces
The launch method is a flywheel or a catapult

checkpoints.gate: No metal is cut before this sign-off.

items.text: Every part of the Design post is filled in, including each role's prototype and calculations
The structure is aluminum, with wood only for a minor part
A process is named for every part
The team uses 6 or fewer 1/2 in hex bearings
The drill or power tool is clamped or mounted to the launcher, never hand-held while firing

checkpoints.title: Design

blocks.prompt: Your launcher is ready for its first full-power shot. Where?
Ana owns Drive. Who can type in the Drive boxes?

criteria.text: Knows where to test and who types where

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Football field, and only the Drive owner.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: One of the two picks is right.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Both wrong, or no picks.

blocks.prompt: How does your idea throw the ball?
Your idea in one line
Photo of your concept sketch
Another page of your sketch (optional)
Stretch: a second concept with a different launch method

criteria.text: The sketch shows how the launcher holds, powers and throws the ball, in a top and a side view

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Top and side view; the ball's path from loading to leaving and the power source are both drawn.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: One view only, or the power source or the ball's path is missing.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No sketch, or not a launcher.

criteria.text: Parts are labeled with sizes and how each is made

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Every major part has a size and a process or stock item.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Some parts are labeled; sizes or processes are missing on others.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No sizes or processes.

blocks.prompt: Ideas A to D: whose sketch, and what it is
Weighted objectives table: criteria, weights, scores and what decided each
Which idea is the team building?
Why it won, with its total
Where the four parts meet

criteria.text: Weighted objectives table: 5 criteria, weights summing to 50, every idea scored, a reason on every criterion

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Five criteria, weights total 50, every idea scored 1 to 5, and every criterion says what decided it.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: One of those is missing: a reason, a score, or the weights do not total 50.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Fewer than five criteria, or several scores or reasons missing.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No table.

criteria.text: The pick is explained by the table, and the interfaces between the four parts are named

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: The reason names the total, or says why the team overrode it; every subsystem's meeting point is named with how they join.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: The reason or the interfaces are vague (no total, or a meeting point missing).

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: A pick with no reason from the table, and interfaces barely named.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: No pick.
